newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Electronics lead Taiwan stocks to 7-yr high close.
newsitem.headline: Electronics lead Taiwan stocks to 7-yr high close.

text.p: Taiwan share prices decisively defied resistance at 9,600 points to notch a seven-year high close on Friday as electronics shares rebounded dramatically from Thursday's late freefall, brokers said.
Brokers cautioned that electronics might see a short-term consolidation soon as the bellwether sector has risen dramatically in the market's recent rally.
The benchmark stock index closed 105.6 points or 1.1 percent higher at 9,677.4, finally succeeding where it had failed in five consecutive attempts -- closing above 9,600 level.
Turnover was very heavy at T$218 billion.

Electronic shares, which tumbled three percent on Thursday in extremely volatile trade, roared back with a 5.21 percent rise -- boosted by motherboard maker Asustek, which rose T$37, the seven percent daily limit, to T$566.
"Electronics were still the most favoured in the day's trade, with more than 50 percent of investment streaming into the sector," said Golden Securities manager Albert Lin.

Brokers said the index was able to sustain a close above technical resistance at 9,600 because the electronics rise did not come at the expense of other sectors. Rather, they said, investors were diversifying holdings across many sectors.
Brokers said investors were not daunted by electronics' huge gain and even more precipitous final-hour fall on Thursday.

"The freefall actually helped the market return to its normal condition," said Lin Long-hsien, assistant manager of United Securities. "It has also brought forth technical rebounds in other sectors that had been neglected in the past few days in the face of red-hot electronics."
Computer giant Acer also was limit up, rising T$7 to T$107. Taiwan Semiconductor gained T$9.5 at T$158.
The index has not closed higher since finishing at 9,713.78 on April 27, 1990.
